title: Resolve cmd.exe and codex to absolute paths before the Codex provider spawns in the delegating workspace
task:
Origin: the Code Safety division's triage of its 2026-09-28 review of this package (data/code-safety/targets/README.md:55, record data/code-safety/2026-09-28-dsh-self-review). No released finding names this defect; the triage found it while reading the code, so this ticket carries the evidence itself.

Problem: `codexAppServerArgv` at packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/run.ts:36-42 returns the bare program names `cmd.exe` and `codex` (`['cmd.exe', '/d', '/s', '/c', 'codex', 'app-server', '--stdio']` on win32, `['codex', ...]` elsewhere), and `startCodexRun` spawns it at packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/run.ts:125-131 with `cwd: spec.cwd`, which `start` sets to the delegating session's workspace at packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/index.ts:67-78. On Windows, libuv's `uv_spawn` passes that explicit cwd to `search_path`, which checks the cwd for a bare file name before any PATH directory (libuv src/win/process.c: "If there's really only a filename, check the current directory for file, then search all path directories"), and `cmd.exe` in turn looks for `codex` in its current directory before PATH. A workspace holding `cmd.exe`, or `codex.cmd`/`codex.bat`/`codex.exe`, therefore runs that file instead of the installed product whenever a session in it delegates to Codex — a cloned repository plants the executable (CWE-427). The README contract at packages/subagent/subagent-codex/README.md:30 ("Production resolves `codex` from `PATH`") holds on POSIX only. The sibling provider already resolves its product through the subprocess seam, which searches PATH only and returns an absolute path: packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code/src/index.ts:112-116.

Required: in `start` (packages/subagent/subagent-codex/src/index.ts), resolve `codex` with `this.ctx.subprocess.resolveExecutable('codex', this.config.env, request.signal)` and, on win32, `cmd.exe` the same way, before anything is spawned; carry the absolute paths in `CodexRunSpec`; make `codexAppServerArgv` take them so that no element of the argv that names a program is a bare file name, while every other element stays constant (no task or configuration text enters the argv). Update the existing argv test at packages/subagent/subagent-codex/tests/subagent-codex.spec.ts:263-274 to the new behavior, and add packages/subagent/subagent-codex/tests/executable-resolution.spec.ts asserting that (a) on win32 the argv's first element and its `codex` element are exactly the absolute paths passed in, (b) on POSIX the first element is the absolute path passed in, and (c) the provider's `start`, over a stub subprocess service that records calls, resolves through `resolveExecutable` before its first `spawn`. State in the README's configuration paragraph (and its Chinese counterpart) that `codex`, and on Windows `cmd.exe`, are resolved from PATH to absolute paths before the spawn, then re-record the pair with `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write packages/subagent/subagent-codex/README.md`.

Constraints: do not change the JSON-RPC wire, the handshake, the approval answers, or packages/subprocess; keep the POSIX argv shape apart from the absolute path. A fix that also needs the ACP or SDK providers is out of scope here: stop and report instead.
